title: Max Subarrays with Mean at Least G

reported.text: Partition the array into the maximum number K of subarrays whose means are all >= G, and output the lexicographically smallest list of lengths (or -1).

sources.passage:
Rubrik OA Question
Given an array arr of length N and an integer G, we want to partition the array into exactly K subarrays such that the mean of the elements in each subarray is >= G. Find the max K possible and print out the lengths of each subarray in their lexicographical order. 

Subarrays of an array can be defined by their starting and ending indexes of an original array. Given an array arr, a subarray of A of arr is less than subarray of B of arr if the starting index of A is less than the starting index of B. If they have the same starting index, then whichever subarray has a smaller ending index lexicographically comes first. For this probleem, since the subarrys partition the original array, they will be non overlapping. 

Output Format : 

If no K is possible, print -1 in the a single line. Otherwise in the first line print a single integer - max K possible. In the second line, print the length of the K subarrays in lexicographical order.

Sample Tests: 
Sample Input 1 : 
5 2 
Sample Output : 
-1 
(since there is no partition possible for any positive K's).

Sample Input 2: 
3 -2 4 6 1

Sample Output: 

2
1 4

Explanation 2 : 
Valid partition present for K =2 (for k>=3 no valid partition is possible). 

For k = 2, the lexicographically smallest partition is [3] and then [-2 4 6 1] is next. Hence, output is 1 (length of [3]) and 4 (length of [-2 4 6 1] ).

Constraints: 
1<= n <= 106 
1<= |arr[i]| , |G| <= 109 
1<= k <= n

Rubrik | Software Engineer | Palo Alto | Sept 2024 [Reject]
YoE: 4

Phone Screen: A variant of this problem - https://leetcode.com/problems/stamping-the-grid/description/. Gave a slightly optimized brute force solution with O(MNXY) and towards the end was able to come up with the concept of prefix sums which would have resulted in O(MN) but I didn't have time to implement this.

I think since I was able to explain the approach well I got selected to the final rounds of interview

Coding Language: Python
Onsite # 1 (System Coding)
Implement a stack using linked list; make it thread-safe. I was able to do this fairly easy and you need to write executable code. Explained some concepts behind concurrency primitives. Later interviewer asked to implement CAS approach - this I couldn't solve. This was asked in the last 10 mins and I had only theoretical knowledge of how it worked so couldn't give a full working solution

Onsite # 2 (Algorithms)
This was a trie question. Not sure if there's a similar problem on leetcode. Each query is of the form "letters""number" . You are a given a list of words. The answer to each query is true or false, which has prefix from the query and has exactly the suffix number of characters following it. List of words = ['ball','apple'] query = ['ba2','app3'] . The result would be [True, False]. I was able to come up with a solution for this. Initially I thought of doing something like this https://leetcode.com/problems/design-add-and-search-words-data-structure/description/. But then the TC would not be linear for the suffix case. Later I came up with an optimal solution by tracking the remaining number of letters in each Trie Node and this worked. All the testcases passed.

Onsite #3 (System Coding)
You are provided 4 functions that operate on blocks of data. You need to write their byte based equivalents and not expose the APIs. The given APIs are block_size(), block_read(), block_write() and block_seek(). Now you need to write seek(location) which seeks to a specific byte location, read(len) read len bytes, and write(buf) which writes len bytes. This was an interesting problem and I had to discuss with the interviewer to understand all the intricacies involved and was able to complete the code as well and the interviewer seemed convinced. Executing this code was not neccessary.

sources.passage:
Rubrik interview experience
Hi community, I recently interviewed at rubrik and I am here to share my interview experience for Software engineer role - India. 

Current company: Microsft, 2.5 YOE

Round 1: System coding 1 [Last week of January]
Implement a bounded thread safe queue. 
Implement a thread pool task executor.
Folllow ups: How to handle exeception in task, how to implement timeout, or reclaim thread.

Round 2: System coding 2 [Last week of January]
Implement reader writer lock. Various cases and how to handle that. Didn't go well so had to give a redo.

Round 3: System coding 3 (redo) [Second week of February]
Memory allocation problem. Implement a thread safe - Car and Truck parking system in a 1-D array where each car takes 1 unit space and a truck takes 2 unit space.

Round 4: DSA [First week of March]
Leetcode problem: https://leetcode.com/problems/count-lattice-points-inside-a-circle/description/ 
With strict constraints. `Number of circles can be 1e3` and `0 <= X, Y <= 1e5`

Round 5: HLD [Second week of March]
Count the highest occurring word in a github across all repository. Infra given is set of VMs and you can run any piece of code on those VMs.

Round 6: Hiring manager round [Third week of March]
Resume discussion and situational questions. 

Verdict: Rejected [Mid April]
Recruiter stated the HM said no due to the less depth in problems I have solved and they don't match to rubrik complexity level. Other techinical rounds went well and had positive feedback. 

*Update: Added timeline*
*PS: The recruiter hinted to take rounds as soon as possible as role gets filled quickly but I wasn't prepared so I took time before each round.*

sources.passage:
SWE (L4) Interview Experience at Rubrik (2025)
I recently attended SWE (L4) Interviews at Rubrik. This post is to give back to the leetcode community. Hope it helps. 

There were a total of 5 rounds:
1. System Coding 1 
2. Algo Coding
3. System Coding 2
4. System Design
5. Hiring Manager and Technical background deep dive.

Rubrik focusses more on multithreading, concurrency and synchronization techniques. Focussing more on these and OS fundamentals helps a lot during interviews. Adding some details for each round and what all I focussed per round.

1. System Coding 1: In this round, they focus on concurrency, multithreading, process, memory management and synchronization concepts. **Question I was asked: **: Design a job scheduler that runs all available jobs in an optimized manner, considering job dependencies. You can assume the existence of a function get_next_jobs(finished_jobs) that returns all jobs whose dependencies are fully satisfied based on the currently finished jobs. A job can only be executed after all of its parent (dependent) jobs are complete. 

2. Algo Coding: Here they ask Medium to Hard level Leetcode question, similar to any other FAANG interviews. **Question I got:** You will receive a stream of data. For each item, return the minimum absolute difference between any two elements among the last K elements in the stream.

3. System Coding 2: There is a playground that can be accessed by only one team at a time, with a maximum of 10 players allowed concurrently. Multiple players from different teams may attempt to access the playground simultaneously. How would you design the system to assign players to the playground while enforcing these constraints?  (They will ask about different approaches you can take to avoid starvation of any player)

4. System Design: Design a system similar to LinkedIn Connections that can answer the query: "How many levels (or degrees) of connection exist between two users?" For example, direct connections are 1st-degree, friends of friends are 2nd-degree, and so on. The system should efficiently handle up to 1 billion users.

5. Hiring Manager and Technical Deep Dive: This round basically focusses on one of the projects you worked on in past (deep dive). You should be aware of all the challenges you faces, decisions you made while working on project etc. They will also ask some behavioral questions.
